Set A  
Product: White can with “Canо Water” and “Still Water” text. Pack: 12 × 500ml in cardboard tray. Can features “Don’t bottle it!” at base. Black flip-top lid visible. One image shows can held by person; another shows can beside ribbed glass. All text legible and consistent.

Set B  
Product: White can with “Canо Water” and “Still Spring Water” text. Pack: 12 × 500ml (Amazon badge visible). Can features “Don’t bottle it!” at base. Black flip-top lid visible. Text on can differs from Set A in water type description.

Agreements  
Both sets show white aluminum cans with black “Canо Water” logo, “Don’t bottle it!” at bottom, and black flip-top lids. Both include a 12-pack tray labeled “12 x 500ml.” Brand name and slogan are identical.

Discrepancies  
Set A labels the product “Still Water”; Set B labels it “Still Spring Water.” The pack count and volume (12 × 500ml) match across both sets. No other attributes (e.g., weight, accessories, variant code) are legible or comparable. The only textual difference is the water type descriptor.

Cannot be determined from images  
Whether “Spring Water” implies a different formulation or regulatory classification cannot be confirmed from visuals alone. No information about ingredients, sourcing, or certifications is visible. The presence of an Amazon badge in Set B does not affect product attributes.

Set A  
Two images: one shows a single 700ml glass bottle of Aperol (blue cap, orange liquid, label reads “Aperol,” “Aperitivo dal 1919,” “Fratelli Barbieri,” “Casa fondata a Padova • Italia”). The second image shows the same bottle beside two glasses labeled “Aperol Spritz,” with orange garnish and ice—lifestyle scene. Product is the classic Aperol aperitif.

Set B  
One image: a four-pack of small glass bottles in an orange cardboard carrier. Label on front reads “Aperol Spritz,” “Ready to Serve,” “4x 20cl,” “With Ice and an Orange Slice.” Each bottle has an orange cap and label stating “Ready to Serve — Chill, Pour, Share.”

Agreements  
Both sets feature the brand name “Aperol” and the word “Spritz” in visual form. Both contain orange-colored liquid. Both are packaged for ready-to-serve consumption.

Discrepancies  
Set A’s product is a single large bottle (no volume visible), labeled as “Aperitivo dal 1919,” with no mention of “Spritz” on the main label. Set B’s product is explicitly “Aperol Spritz,” sold as a 4-pack of 20cl bottles (total 80cl). The packaging design, bottle shape, cap color, and labeling content differ significantly. Set A’s bottle is tall and ribbed; Set B’s are short, uniform, and sealed with orange caps.

Cannot be determined from images  
The exact volume of the Set A bottle is not legible on the label. Whether the Set B “20cl” refers to each bottle or total pack is unambiguous but not confirmed by visual text alone—though “4x 20cl” implies per-bottle volume. No information about formulation differences (e.g., added soda, sugar) is visible.
